The criteria proposed by the International Association of the Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups (IADPSG) for screening gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) are considered cost-effective. 

The IADPSG criteria, which recommend a one-step approach using a 75-gram oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) with a single threshold of 92 mg/dL for fasting plasma glucose, 180 mg/dL for 1-hour plasma glucose, and 153 mg/dL for 2-hour plasma glucose, have been shown to be cost-effective in preventing adverse pregnancy outcomes. 

Cost-effectiveness analyses have demonstrated that the IADPSG criteria are cost-effective, particularly when considering the long-term benefits of reducing the risk of complications associated with GDM, such as macrosomia, cesarean delivery, and future development of type 2 diabetes in both the mother and the child. 

However, the cost-effectiveness may vary depending on the specific healthcare setting, population, and available resources. Nevertheless, the IADPSG criteria are widely accepted and recommended by many professional organizations as a cost-effective approach to screening for GDM.
